title: Scholten Japanese Art opens Asia Week exhibition featuring rediscovered collection
summary: Scholten Japanese Art opened their Asia Week Autumn 2026 exhibition, Rediscovered Treasures: The León Chattah Collection of Modern Japanese Prints. The exhibition includes a group of seventy works by 20th century shin hanga masters from the ‘hidden’ collection of León Chattah (1934-2025). Recently rediscovered by his family, this significant collection had been tucked away in the back of a closet in a New York City apartment since the early 1980s. The entire collection was acquired (purportedly all at once), from Abraham & Rachel Bornstein, the proprietors of the Boston Book and Art Shop, founded in 1923. Located at 657 Boylston Street across from the Boston Public Library, the shop specialized in distributing books from leading European publishers, as well as independently publishing fine books, art portfolios and monographs. title: Jean-Michel Basquiat and Yayoi Kusama lead Christie's evening sale at The Henderson

title: Morphy's announces October petroliana, automobilia, and vintage advertising sale
summary: A 1906 Indian Camelback motorized bicycle built by The Hendee Manufacturing Company (later The Indian Motorcycle Company, with no “R” in motocycle), a circa 1930s Sinclair Aircraft double-sided porcelain sign with iconic airplane graphics, and a 1932 Cadillac 355-B seven-passenger Imperial limousine registered to notorious gangster Al Capone share top billing in Morphy’s October 4 Automobilia, Petroliana & Advertising auction. The auction is packed with more than 650 lots of motoring-related signage, service station items and vehicles certain to please collectors at every price point. The event will be held live at Morphy’s Pennsylvania gallery, with all forms of remote bidding available, including live via the internet through Morphy Live. title: Meet Nomad Studios: A New Way to Discover Contemporary African Art
summary: There is a lot of exciting contemporary art being created across Africa today, but discovering it from outside the continent is not always easy. While international interest in African artists continues to grow, many emerging creatives remain relatively unknown to audiences and collectors in Europe and elsewhere. Nomad Studios is a new initiative looking to make those connections a little easier—and, in the process, encourage a broader conversation about what contemporary African art can be. Born in Africa and working across Africa and Europe, Nomad Studios brings together emerging artists whose work reflects the many different ways of being African today. Its online marketplace offers international audiences an opportunity to discover and collect work from artists at an earlier stage of their careers, while its wider creative agency works with artists on commissioned projects, commercial collaborations and creative partnerships. title: The Frick names Caitlin Henningsen Head of Education and Public Engagement
summary: The Frick Collection announced the appointment of Caitlin Henningsen as its new Ayesha Bulchandani Head of Education and Public Engagement. She takes up the role at the helm of the institution’s Education Department starting September 21, 2026. Commented Axel Rüger, Anna-Maria and Stephen Kellen Director, “The Frick’s education program has long been a cornerstone of our mission. It has evolved and grown substantially over the years thanks to a cohort of deeply committed staff members, in which Caitlin has played an increasingly essential role. Since our recent renovation and reopening, her expertise and creativity have been vital as we reintroduce the Frick’s programming and activate our new purpose-built education spaces. title: Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III announces retirement
summary: Lonnie G. Bunch III, the 14th Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, announced today he will retire from his position, concluding nearly 38 years of service at the Smithsonian and a career that has shaped the museum field in the United States and beyond. “It is with very mixed emotions and heartfelt gratitude that I announce my retirement from the Smithsonian,” Bunch said. “I have spent nearly half of my life working at and being part of the Smithsonian family, and what a privilege it has been. There is no place like the Smithsonian—it has been one of the great loves of my life, and I am extraordinarily proud of what we have accomplished together. I leave with pride and sadness, gratitude and joy, and with enormous confidence in the people who will carry this remarkable institution forward.” Bunch was named Secretary in June 2019, making him the first African American and first historian to serve in the role in the Smithsonian’s history. title: Christie's to auction $40m Radiant Modernism collection across London, Paris, and New York
summary: Christie's announced Radiant Modernism, a Private European Collection of late 19th- to 20th-century art spanning paintings, works on paper and prints, which will be offered across multiple sales and regions from October 2026 throughout 2027. With an overall estimate in the region of $40,000,000 -60,000,000, Radiant Modernism will be presented in different auction rooms, starting in London during Frieze Week, then travelling to Paris for Art Basel and subsequently to New York during its November Marquee Week, with further sales in 2027. Assembled privately over forty years and comprising nearly 600 works, Radiant Modernism stands out for its rarity, quality and the academic rigour underpinning its acquisition. Three principal strands can be identified within the collection: Pointillism, represented predominantly by Paul Signac; Symbolism, with a number of rare works by Odilon Redon; and Expressionism, represented by artists including Lyonel Feininger. title: Maruani Mercier presents Jonathan Lasker exhibition surveying four decades of oil studies
summary: Maruani Mercier presents Jonathan Lasker: A Survey of the Maquettes 1986-2026, a selection of important works in oil on paper spanning nearly four decades of the artist’s practice. Invariably executed on a small scale with painstaking precision, Lasker’s earliest fully rendered ‘maquettes’ or ‘studies’ date from 1986 and have since occupied an essential place in his process. Underpinning some of the key large-scale paintings, the studies in the exhibition form a standalone body of work and offer insight into the dialectic of planning and spontaneity inherent to Lasker’s artistic production. The introduction of oil studies in the mid-1980s coincided with the consolidation of Lasker’s highly reflective conceptual approach to painting. title: Christie's to offer Monsoon founder Peter Simon's art collection during London Marquee Week
summary: Christie's will present Monsoon: The Peter Simon Collection, highlighting its London Marquee Week in October 2026. Offered in three dedicated auctions with an Evening Sale, a Day Sale plus an online sale collectively comprising nearly 200 works, this selection from the personal collection of British businessman Peter Simon, the founder of Monsoon, will be offered during Frieze Week when international art market attention turns to London, and represents the highest value single-owner collection offered to date at Christie's London in a single Marquee Week. The Peter Simon Collection stands as one of Britain's foremost Modern and Contemporary Art collections. It embodies the same wide-ranging curiosity, intuitive selection, and global perspective that has defined the career of Peter Simon, founder of Monsoon, the renowned international fashion brand. title: Heritage Auctions appoints Whitney Maxwell Chief Marketing Officer
summary: Heritage Auctions announces the appointment of Whitney Maxwell as Chief Marketing Officer, effective Oct. 5. Based in Heritage’s New York and Dallas offices, Maxwell will lead the company’s global marketing strategy, overseeing brand development, digital initiatives, client engagement and campaigns across Heritage’s more than 50 collecting categories. Maxwell brings more than 15 years of experience driving growth in the art and auction industry, with a career spanning marketing, digital strategy, operations and business leadership. She most recently served as Managing Director of Bonhams|Cars, the auction house’s global motoring division, where she held full profit-and-loss responsibility. summary: Powerhouse Arts (PHA), the Brooklyn-based nonprofit, today announced the appointment of Cathy Harding as Vice President of Institutional Advancement. title: Speed Art Museum names Kathleen V. Jameson, Ph.D., as new Director
summary: The Speed Art Museum today announced the appointment of Kathleen V. Jameson, Ph.D., as its new Director. Jameson officially began her role on September 8. A museum leader, scholar, and arts advocate with more than three decades of experience, Jameson brings extensive expertise in museum leadership, curatorial work, fundraising, strategic planning, and community engagement. As Kentucky’s oldest and largest art museum, the Speed has served as an important cultural institution for Louisville and the Commonwealth for nearly a century. Jameson joins the Museum at a significant moment as the Speed approaches its 100th anniversary in 2027 and looks ahead to its next century of service, scholarship, and community connection. “Dr. Jameson brings exactly the combination of experience, vision and leadership we believe the Speed needs at this important moment,” said John Crockett, Chair

title: Christie's to offer art collection of music mogul Clive Davis
summary: Christie's will present the collection of Clive Davis, the legendary record executive who was instrumental in pioneering the landscape of American music for more than 60 years. Eight artworks from Mr. Davis's collection will headline the 20th Century Evening Sale, the premier event of November's Fall Marquee Week, with additional works in the Post-War and Contemporary Art Day Sale in November and in the Prints and Multiples sale in October. Mr. Davis is widely considered the most significant and influential music executive of the 20th and early 21st centuries with a unique talent and an unrivaled “ear” for hits. title: Belgian artist Lisa Vlaemminck debuts new shaped paintings in Brussels
summary: With Dressage Ruined by Puffers, Belgian artist Lisa Vlaemminck presents a new series of shaped paintings at rodolphe janssen. Cut from wood into recognisable silhouettes—a tooth, a hairstyle, a slice of cheese, a chicken leg—the works establish a relation between the physical form of the support and the image painted onto it. The two do not necessarily correspond. A recognisable contour can carry an unrelated image, while the image can alter how the contour is perceived. In Vlaemminck’s work, shape and subject enter into an oblique relationship, sometimes echoing one another, but more often refusing to line up. Familiar forms operate almost like visual fragments or signs, while the paintings remain elusive. What initially appears legible becomes strange through a shift in scale, context or meaning. summary: This September, the KINDL – Centre for Contemporary Art in Berlin will open four new exhibitions as part of Berlin Art Week 2026: Mischa Kuball. boiler house (Kesselhaus), Kira Freije. Between Sunlight (Maschinenhaus M1), NEOZOON. together (M1 VideoSpace), and Thu-Van Tran. Write As Beasts Scream at Night (Maschinenhaus M2). title: Royal College of Art announces dynamic line-up for London Design Festival 2026
summary: A dynamic line-up of exhibitions, pop-ups, and collaborative showcases sees Royal College of Art (RCA) students, researchers, and alumni present their works to the public and the international design community during the 24th annual London Design Festival (12–20 September 2026). From student-led showcases tackling contemporary design challenges to major alumni exhibitions and research-driven museum interventions, RCA creators continue to shape the global design landscape. InResponse in the Brompton Design District brings together 30 graduating designers from the RCA’s MA Design Products programme, presenting design as an active form of enquiry rather than simply an act of object-making. summary: The Smithsonian's Archives of American Art has named the distinguished honorees for its upcoming annual fall gala. title: Grande Brera announces expansive 2026-27 season spanning Hayez to Marina Abramović
summary: Grande Brera is preparing for one of its most expansive seasons yet, bringing together painting, literature, digital art and institutional history in a 2026–27 program that stretches from the Romanticism of Francesco Hayez to the performance legacy of Marina Abramović. Rather than functioning as a series of separate exhibitions, the season is designed to bring the various institutions that make up Grande Brera into closer conversation. The Pinacoteca di Brera, Palazzo Citterio, Biblioteca Nazionale Braidense and Brera Academy of Fine Arts will each contribute exhibitions that move between historical collections and contemporary artistic practice. title: Gilbert Portanier exhibition in Cannes highlights pioneer of painterly ceramics
summary: One hundred years after the birth of Gilbert Portanier, Cannes and Vallauris are celebrating an artist who spent much of his life dissolving the boundary between painting and ceramics. Across September, the two French Riviera towns are bringing his work back into focus through exhibitions, the opening of his longtime studio, a public conversation and the publication of a new biography. Portanier, who was born in Cannes on September 28, 1926, and died in Golfe-Juan in 2023, arrived in Vallauris in 1948, at a moment when the town was becoming an international center for artists working in ceramics. He had trained as a painter, and that background would shape everything that followed: rather than treating clay simply as a material for pottery, he approached it as another surface for color, line and image. title: Heritage's September 25 Fine & Rare Wine auction offers extraordinary depth from California to Bordeaux
summary: Serious wine collectors know that a great cellar is defined not simply by individual trophy bottles, but by depth: the opportunity to follow an estate across vintages, trace the evolution of a legendary producer and experience extraordinary wines at different stages of maturity. Heritage Auctions’ September 25 Fine & Rare Wine Signature® Auction offers that opportunity on a remarkable scale. The 660-lot event brings together exceptional depth from California and the Old World, including 26 vintages of Dominus, 52 lots of Harlan Estate, 24 lots of Scarecrow and 41 lots from Screaming Eagle. title: Alfred Ehrhardt Stiftung presents Ramona Schacht exhibition on industrial photography
summary: The Alfred Ehrhardt Stiftung presents for the first time the historical industrial photographs of Alfred Ehrhardt (1901–84) in an entirely new, contemporary light. From 1954 to 1963, Ehrhardt produced numerous films and photographic works on commission for the tobacco company Reemtsma & Co. These works have remained largely underrecognized and stand in contrast to his well-known artistic photographs of nature and landscapes. The documents, which have rarely been exhibited, form the foundation for Leipzig-based artist Ramona Schacht’s (b. 1989) latest work: Photography’s Claim to Property. Bilder im Auftrag Reemtsmas.
